messages.subject: Understanding standardized estimates from partialInvarianceCat()
parts:
Hello all,

I'm conducting measurement invariance tests with ordered categorical indicators across two groups using measEq.syntax() and following up with partialInvarianceCat() to get a sense of effect sizes. The standardized estimates for my factor loadings in partialInvarianceCat() seem quite large and are very different from the completely standardized solutions in the normal model results. I'm trying to understand the cause of this difference and whether I can trust the partialInvarianceCat() results enough to present them.

Here's the code I used to estimate the configural and metric models and to get the partial invariance estimates:

model <- '
L =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6
x1 ~~ x6
x5 ~~ x6
'

model_baseline <-  as.character(measEq.syntax(configural.model =
                              model,
                              data = data,
                              ordered = c("x1", "x2", "x3","x4",
                                          "x5", "x6"),
                              parameterization = "theta",
                              ID.fac = "std.lv",
                              ID.cat = "Joreskog",
                              group = "g",
                              group.equal = "configural"))

fit_baseline <- cfa(model = model_baseline, data = data,   
                        group = "g",
                        ordered = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4",
                                    "x5", "x6"),
                        parameterization = "theta")

model_loadings <- as.character(measEq.syntax(configural.model =  
                                model,
                                data = data,
                                ordered = c("x1", "x2",  
                                "x3","x4", "x5", "x6"),
                                parameterization = "theta",
                                ID.fac = "std.lv",
                                ID.cat = "Joreskog",
                                group = "g",
                                group.equal = "loadings"))

fit_loadings <- cfa(model = model_loadings, data = data, 
                        group = "g",
                         ordered = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4",
                                     "x5", "x6"),
                         parameterization = "theta")

modelsCat <- list(fit.configural = fit_baseline, fit.loadings = fit_loadings)

partialInvarianceCat(modelsCat, type = "metric")

Based on Sunthud Pornprasertmanit's (2022) vignette on the effect size calculations, I would have thought these estimates of the standardized loadings would look more similar to the std.all in the configural model. But they are much larger (and more similar to std.lv).

Why would partialInvarianceCat() produce such large standardized loadings? And are they "incorrect" such that I shouldn't report them?

Thank you,
Micah
